rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi treats the conditional as part of what was revealed to Muhammad, a second item revealed after the jinn listened.
rows.anchor: هذا من جملة الموحى إليه والتقدير : قل أوحي إلي أنه استمع نفر وأن لو استقاموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن is a reduced form of أن الثقيلة: the sense is that, had they been upright, such-and-such would have followed.
rows.anchor: أن ) مخففة من الثقيلة والمعنى : وأوحي إلي أن الشأن والحديث لو استقاموا

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi compares separating لو from its verb to separating لا and the future marker in cited constructions.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : وفصل لو بينها وبين الفعل كفصل لا والسين في

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view takes the pronoun in استقاموا to refer to the previously described jinn; uprightness would bring them abundant water.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : إلى الجن الذين تقدم ذكرهم ووصفهم ، أي هؤلاء القاسطون

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others take the pronoun to mean humans: abundant water is a fitting inducement for people, not jinn.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل المراد الإنس ، واحتجوا عليه بوجهين الأول

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: The human-reference view also appeals to the years when God withheld rain from Mecca before the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: أن هذه الآية إنما نزلت بعدما حبس الله المطر عن أهل مكة سنين

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi says the pronoun encompasses both jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: وقال القاضي : الأقرب أن الكل يدخلون فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi supports the inclusive reading: a ruling attached to a cause, uprightness, applies wherever that cause occurs.
rows.anchor: يمكن أن يحتج لصحة قول القاضي بأنه تعالى لما أثبت حكما معللا بعلة وهو الاستقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غدق means abundant water; its dāl is read with either fatḥa or kasra, and the word also describes plentiful rain.
rows.anchor: الغدق بفتح الدال وكسرها : الماء الكثير ، وقرىء بهما يقال : غدقت العين بالكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first interpretation of ماء غدق is rainfall.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أنه الغيث والمطر ، والثاني

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim interprets the abundant water as an allusion to Paradise, as in the description of gardens beneath which rivers flow.
rows.anchor: وهو قول أبي مسلم : أنه إشارة إلى الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation makes water a metaphor for worldly benefits and good things, since water is their source.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : أنه المنافع والخيرات جعل الماء كناية عنها ، لأن الماء أصل الخيرات كلها في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If استقاموا refers to jinn, one reading means their forefather remained in worship, did not refuse to prostrate to Adam or disbelieve, and his descendants followed Islam; water signifies good living.
rows.anchor: لو ثبت أبوهم الجان على ما كان عليه من عبادة الله ولم يستكبر عن السجود لآدم ولم يكفر وتبعه ولده على الإسلام

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj selects the first jinn interpretation because the definite article in الطريقة points to the familiar path of guidance.
rows.anchor: واختار الزجاج الوجه الأول قال : لأنه تعالى ذكر الطريقة معرفة بالألف واللام فتكون راجعة إلى الطريقة المعروفة المشهورة وهي طريقة الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second jinn reading says the Quran-hearing jinn would have received expanded provision had they stayed on their former path instead of converting.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المعنى وأن لو استقام الجن الذين سمعوا القرآن على طريقتهم التي كانوا عليها قبل الاستماع ولم ينتقلوا عنها إلى الإسلام

rows.speaker: أصحاب التأويل الثاني
rows.claim: Supporters of the second reading cite the following phrase about testing them and compare it to God extending respite so people increase in sin.
rows.anchor: الذاهبون إلى التأويل الثاني استدلوا عليه بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that prosperity given to believers also tests gratitude and whether they spend it in seeking God's pleasure or in pursuing desire and Satan.
rows.anchor: أن من آمن فأنعم الله عليه كان ذلك الإنعام أيضا ابتلاء واختبارا حتى يظهر أنه هل يشتغل بالشكر أم لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the pronoun refers to humans, the same two interpretations apply, but taking the water literally is more fitting because humans benefit from it more fully.
rows.anchor: وأما الذين قالوا : الضمير عائد إلى الإنس ، فالوجهان عائدان فيه بعينه

rows.speaker: ابن قطيب
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba reads حسابا with a doubled consonant, taking it as المحسب (that which is reckoned), like دراك for المدرك, as al-Kashshaf reports.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن قطيب : { حسابا } بالتشديد على أن الحساب بمعنى المحسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the punishment of unbelievers and reward of the God-fearing, Razi says the passage concludes by affirming God's lordship and that creatures possess no right to address Him.
rows.anchor: لما بالغ في وصف وعيد الكفار ووعد المتقين ، ختم الكلام

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafi, and Abu Amr read both رب and الرحمن in the nominative.
rows.anchor: الرفع فيهما وهو قراءة ابن كثير ونافع وأبي عمرو

rows.speaker: عاصم وعبدالله بن عامر
rows.claim: Asim and Abdullah ibn Amir read both words in the genitive.
rows.anchor: والجر فيهما وهو قراءة عاصم وعبدالله بن عامر

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read رب in the genitive and الرحمن in the nominative.
rows.anchor: والجر في الأول مع الرفع في الثاني ، وهو قراءة حمزة والكسائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With both words nominative, one parse makes رب السماوات the subject and الرحمن its predicate.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أن يكون رب السموات مبتدأ ، والرحمن خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another nominative parse makes الرحمن an adjective of رب السماوات and لا يملكون its predicate.
rows.anchor: رب السموات مبتدأ ، والرحمن صفة ولا يملكون خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third nominative parse supplies an omitted subject: هو رب السماوات هو الرحمن, then begins a new clause.
rows.anchor: أن يضمر المبتدأ والتقدير هو :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth nominative parse treats الرحمن and لا يملكون as two predicates.
rows.anchor: ورابعها : أن يكون { الرحمان } و { لا يملكون } خبرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genitive reading makes the words an appositive of ربك.
rows.anchor: وأما وجه الجر فعلى البدل من ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the mixed reading, رب is genitive as an appositive of ربك, while الرحمن is nominative as a subject whose predicate is لا يملكون.
rows.anchor: جر الأول بالبدل من ربك ، والثاني مرفوع بكونه مبتدأ وخبره لا يملكون

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: One view makes the pronoun refer to polytheists, who cannot address God, while believers may intercede and God accepts it.
rows.anchor: نقل عطاء عن ابن عباس إنه راجع إلى المشركين يريد لا يخاطب المشركون أما المؤمنون فيشفعون

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi says the pronoun refers to believers: God's just punishment and reward leave them no grounds to address Him as claimants.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : إنه راجع إلى المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi judges al-Qadi's reading closer than the first because the preceding passage spoke of believers rather than unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول أقرب من الأول لأن الذي جرى قبل هذه الآية ذكر المؤمنين لا ذكر الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi's preferred reading makes the pronoun refer to all inhabitants of heaven and earth: no creature owns the right to address God.
rows.anchor: أنه ضمير لأهل السموات والأرض ، وهذا هو الصواب ، فإن أحدا من المخلوقين لا يملك مخاطبة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Authorized intercession does not contradict this reading: what God grants through grace is not something the intercessor owns.
rows.anchor: وأما الشفاعات الواقعة بإذنه فغير واردة على هذا الكلام لأنه نفى الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: First rational proof: all things besides God belong to Him, and an owned creature has no entitlement against its owner; this reasoning follows Sunni premises.
rows.anchor: أن كل ما سواء فهو مملوكه والمملوك لا يستحق على مالكه شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Second proof: an obligation on God would make Him liable to blame or praise and deficient, needing completion by another; this too follows Sunni premises.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : أن معنى الاستحقاق عليه ، هو أنه لو لم يفعل لاستحق الذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Third proof, based on Mu'tazilite premises: God knows evil is evil and has no need of it, so He does not commit it; no one can demand an explanation from Him.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : أنه عالم بقبح القبيح ، عالم بكونه غنيا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the next verse reinforces the claim that no creature can address God or demand anything from Him, by describing the speechless assembly on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر أن أحدا من الخلق لا يمكنه أن يخاطب الله في شيء أو يطالبه بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels are the greatest creatures in rank and power, yet remain silent at Resurrection out of reverence, fear, and submission to their Lord; the state of others is even clearer.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأن الملائكة أعظم المخلوقات قدرا ورتبة

rows.speaker: أصحاب تفضيل الملك على البشر
rows.claim: Those who rank angels above humans use this verse: if angels are awed before God's majesty, lesser beings must be still more so; the argument assumes angels are creation's noblest.
rows.anchor: لمن يقول بتفضيل الملك على البشر أن يتمسك بهذه الآية

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud identifies the Spirit as an angel greater than the heavens and mountains.
rows.anchor: فعن ابن مسعود أنه ملك أعظم من السموات والجبال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the Spirit as one of the greatest angels in created stature.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس هو ملك من أعظم الملائكة خلقا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the Spirit is a creation shaped like human descendants, who eat and drink but are not human beings.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد : خلق على / صورة بني آدم

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada interpret the Spirit as human beings, meaning those possessing a spirit.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن وقتادة هم بنو آدم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas identifies the Spirit as human souls.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أرواح الناس

rows.speaker: الضحاك والشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Shabi identify the Spirit as Gabriel.
rows.anchor: وعن الضحاك والشعبي هو جبريل عليه السلام

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi prefers Gabriel: the Quran uses this name for him, and Gabriel can stand, speak, and receive permission, unlike an unknown creature or the Quran itself.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول هو المختار عند القاضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صفا may mean the Spirit and all angels stand as one row, as two rows, or as multiple rows.
rows.anchor: أما قوله : { صفا } فيحتمل أن يكون المعنى

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The apparent exegetical view is that the Spirit stands alone as one row and all the angels form another, reflecting the Spirit's great stature against their ranks.
rows.anchor: وظاهر قول المفسرين أنهم يقومون صفين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view has the Spirit and angels standing in many rows, as in the description of the angels in al-Fajr.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : بل يقومون صفوفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of ثم أدبر يسعى says Pharaoh fled in terror after seeing the serpent; al-Hasan calls him reckless and quick-moving.
rows.anchor: أنه لما رأى الثعبان أدبر مرعوبا يسعى يسرع في مشيه ، قال الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading says Pharaoh turned away from Moses while striving to plot against him.
rows.anchor: تولى عن موسى يسعى ويجتهد في مكايدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading takes أدبر as began to act or proceed, like أقبل يفعل; أدبر avoids describing Pharaoh as approaching.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المعنى ، ثم أقبل يسعى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh gathered the magicians as in al-Shuara, then proclaimed his claim at their gathering, sent an announcer to proclaim it, or addressed the people himself.
rows.anchor: فحشر فجمع السحرة كقوله : { فأرسل فرعون فى المدائن حاشرين }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Pharaoh's first claim was that he knew no god for the people besides himself, and his final one was that he was their highest lord.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس كلمته الأولى :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects the literal idea that Pharaoh believed himself creator of the cosmos, since its falsity is self-evident; one who doubts this is insane, and God would not send prophets to an insane person.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز أن يعتقد الإنسان في نفسه كونه خالقا للسموات والأرض والجبال والنبات والحيوان والإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says Pharaoh was a materialist denying a Creator and resurrection, claiming only he could command or forbid; ربكم meant your nurturer and benefactor, since he denied any deity or messenger.
rows.anchor: بل الرجل كان دهريا منكرا للصانع والحشر والنشر

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi says that after the staff became a serpent and exposed Pharaoh's helplessness, his claim to be the highest lord was incongruous; he seemed deranged and unaware of his words.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : وقد كان الأليق به بعد ظهور خزيه عند انقلاب العصا حية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recounting Pharaoh's deeds and words, Razi says the text next recounts how God dealt with him: He seized him as a lesson for the latter and former generations.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى لما حكى عنه أفعاله وأقواله أتبعه بما عامله به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the surah lists twelve events; once they occur, every soul will know what it has brought forth, and the first event is the sun's being wrapped up.
rows.anchor: ذكر اثني عشر شيئا ، وقال : إذا وقعت هذه الأشياء فهنالك { علمت نفس ما أحضرت } [ التكوير : 14 ] . فالأول : قوله تعالى : { إذا الشمس كورت }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first lexical meaning of تكوير is winding or wrapping around, as one winds a turban; الحور بعد الكور means dispersion after cohesion.
rows.anchor: في التكوير وجهان : أحدهما : التلفيف على جهة الاستدارة كتكوير العمامة ، وفي الحديث :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Twisting, rolling, and تكوير are equivalent; a barber's roll is named كارة because clothes are gathered into one garment.
rows.anchor: والطي واللف والكور والتكوير واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because a wrapped object disappears from sight, تكوير describes removing the sun's light and making it unseen.
rows.anchor: ثم إن الشيء الذي يلف لا شك أنه يصير مختفيا عن الأعين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One reported interpretation is that the sun is blotted out; others say it is eclipsed.
rows.anchor: فلهذا قال بعضهم : كورت أي طمست

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the event as the sun's light being erased.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : محي ضوؤها

rows.speaker: المفضل بن سلمة
rows.claim: Al-Mufaddal ibn Salama says the sun's light will depart as though it were hidden inside a roll.
rows.anchor: وقال المفضل بن سلمة : كورت أي ذهب ضوؤها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second lexical possibility is that تكوير means hurling down: the sun is cast away from its orbit.
rows.anchor: الوجه الثاني : في التكوير يقال : كورت الحائط ودهورته إذا طرحته حتى يسقط

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Asmai uses كوره for knocking someone down with a spear, supporting the sense that the sun is thrown from its orbit.
rows.anchor: قال الأصمعي : يقال طعنه فكوره إذا صرعه

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: A third report from Umar derives the word from Persian: كور is said of a blind person.
rows.anchor: يروى عن عمر أنه لفظة مأخوذة من الفارسية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the conditional construction, الشمس is a grammatical subject raised by an implicit verb explained by كورت, since إذا calls for a verb through its conditional sense.
rows.anchor: الجواب : بل على الفاعلية رافعها فعل مضمر

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra's report, transmitted through Abu Salama, says the sun and moon will be two rolled-up bulls in Hell on Resurrection Day; Hasan asked what sin they had committed, and Abu Salama replied that he was reporting the Messenger's words.
rows.anchor: فحدث عن أبي هريرة أنه عليه السلام قال : إن الشمس والقمر ثوران مكوران في النار يوم القيامة قال الحسن : وما ذنبهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says Hasan's objection fails: the sun and moon are inanimate, so fire cannot harm them; they may intensify Hell's heat, making the report rationally possible.
rows.anchor: أن سؤال الحسن ساقط ، لأن الشمس والقمر جمادان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stars will scatter and fall, as in al-Infitar; the root sense of انكدار is pouring down.
rows.anchor: أي تناثرت وتساقطت كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil explains انكدر عليهم القول as people arriving in successive groups and pouring over someone, illustrating the root sense of pouring.
rows.anchor: قال الخليل : يقال انكدر عليهم القول إذا جاءوا أرسالا فانصبوا عليهم

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the sky will rain stars, leaving none in the heavens without falling to earth.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي : تمطر السماء يومئذ نجوما فلا يبقى نجم في السماء إلا وقع على وجه الأرض

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says stars hang like lanterns between heaven and earth on chains of light held by angels; when the inhabitants die, the chains fall from angelic hands.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء : وذلك أنها في قناديل معلقة بين السماء والأرض بسلاسل من النور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains will be moved away from the earth's surface, as in al-Naba, or moved through the air like passing clouds, as in al-Naml.
rows.anchor: أو في الهواء كقوله : { تمر مر السحاب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard interpretation of العشار is pregnant camels in their tenth month, a prized possession; عطلت means their owners abandon them amid Resurrection's terrors, as Ibn Abbas says.
rows.anchor: المشهور أن ( العشار ) جمع عشراء كالنفاس في جمع نفساء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the pregnant camels are neglected because people are consumed by that day's terrors.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : أهملها أهلها لما جاءهم من أهوال يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The camel image addresses Arabs, whose wealth and livelihood depended on camels; it depicts property becoming useless and everyone occupied with himself.
rows.anchor: وخوطب العرب بأمر العشار لأن أكثر مالها وعيشها من الإبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi links the abandonment of wealth to the verses saying wealth and children will not benefit except for a sound heart and that people will come alone.
rows.anchor: والغرض من ذلك ذهاب الأموال وبطلان الأملاك ، واشتغال الناس بأنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes العشار as clouds emptied of their water; although metaphorical, it fits the surrounding signs better.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : أن العشار كناية عن السحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cloud interpretation draws support from the Arabs' comparison of clouds to pregnant carriers, as in al-Dhariyat.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فالعرب تشبه السحاب بالحامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وحش means untamed land animals, and حشرت means gathered from every direction.
rows.anchor: كل شيء من دواب البر مما لا يستأنس فهو وحش

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says every creature, even flies, will be gathered so that retaliation can be carried out.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : يحشر كل شيء حتى الذباب للقصاص

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazila say all animals will be resurrected so God can compensate them for suffering through death, killing, and other harms; afterward He may keep some in Paradise or annihilate them according to the report.
rows.anchor: قال المعتزلة : إن الله تعالى يحشر الحيوانات كلها في ذلك اليوم ليعوضها على آلامها التي وصلت إليها في الدنيا بالموت والقتل

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Razi's school says God has no obligation of compensation by entitlement; He gathers the animals, gives the hornless justice against the horned, then tells them to die and they do.
rows.anchor: وأما أصحابنا فعندهم أنه لا يجب على الله شيء بحكم الاستحقاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The animal gathering demonstrates that if God gathers animals to manifest justice, it is incoherent to deny resurrection to accountable humans and jinn.
rows.anchor: إذا كان [ يوم القيامة ] يحشر كل الحيوانات إظهارا للعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wild animals normally flee people and disperse in deserts, so their assembly with humans shows the overwhelming terror of that day.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أنها تجتمع في موقف القيامة مع شدة نفرتها عن الناس في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Predator and prey will neither gather to eat nor attack one another, which Razi attributes to the day's terror.
rows.anchor: والثالث : أن هذه الحيوانات بعضها غذاء للبعض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another view from Ibn Abbas takes the animals' gathering to mean their death; Arabic also says a harsh year gathered people when it devastated them.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية قول آخر لابن عباس وهو أن حشر الوحوش عبارة عن موتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb حشرت is also read with a doubled consonant.
rows.anchor: وقرئ حشرت بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سجرت is read with either a light or doubled consonant; one explanation derives it from kindling an oven, drying the water so the seas become intensely hot and burning.
rows.anchor: قرئ بالتخفيف والتشديد ، وفيه وجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the drying interpretation, the earth may swell upward to the mountain tops, or crushed mountain debris may fill lowlands until the earth lies level with the seas.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون الأرض لما نشفت مياه البحار ربت فارتفعت

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi reads سجرت as flooded or burst open: God removes the barrier between seas so their waters merge into one.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : أن يكون { سجرت }

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal's third reading takes سجرت as kindled: Hell lies beneath sea beds and its fire ignites the waters when the world ends; alternatively God casts celestial bodies into seas or creates great fires there.
rows.anchor: قال القفال : وهذا التأويل يحتمل وجوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls those mechanisms strained and unnecessary: God can heat the seas or turn their waters into fire directly, without casting in the sun, moon, and stars or placing Hell beneath them.
rows.anchor: وأقول هذه الوجوه متكلفة لا حاجة إلى شيء منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barrier between two seas is described in al-Rahman.
rows.anchor: مرج البحرين يلتقيان ، بينهما برزخ لا يبغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first six signs may occur when the world begins to be destroyed or after Resurrection has begun; the wording does not decide, while the remaining six belong specifically to Resurrection.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن هذه العلامات الست يمكن وقوعها في أول زمان تخريب الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says souls are joined to bodies.
rows.anchor: أحدها : قرنت الأرواح بالأجساد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says people will become three groups, as described in al-Waqia.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : يصيرون فيها ثلاثة أزواج كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation pairs people with others in their rank: the foremost in obedience with their like, the middling with their like, and sinners with their like.
rows.anchor: أنه يضم كل صنف من كان في طبقته من الرجال والنساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth interpretation pairs each man with the angel and authority attached to him; the cited command gathers wrongdoers with their spouses, explained as devils.
rows.anchor: يضم كل رجل إلى من كان يلزمه من ملك وسلطان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says believers' souls are paired with houris and unbelievers' souls with devils.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : زوجت نفوس المؤمنين بالحور العين وقرنت نفوس الكافرين بالشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view pairs each person with their community or sect, such as Jews with Jews and Christians with Christians; a Prophetic report supports it.
rows.anchor: قرن كل امرئ بشيعته اليهودي باليهودي والنصراني بالنصراني

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says souls will be paired with their deeds.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : قرنت النفوس بأعمالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وأد is a metathesized form of آد, meaning to burden; burying a girl under earth was a burdening act, as in the verse about the heavens not being wearied.
rows.anchor: وأد يئد مقلوب من آد يئود أودا ثقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One described custom dressed a newborn girl in wool or hair clothes to herd livestock; if her father chose to kill her, he dressed her for a visit, took her to a prepared pit, pushed her in, and covered her.
rows.anchor: ألبسها جبة من صوف أو شعر لترعى له الإبل والغنم في البادية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says a pregnant woman dug a pit before delivery, gave birth over it, discarded a girl in it, and kept a boy.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كانت الحامل إذا قربت حفرت حفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reasons for killing daughters included fear of family disgrace and poverty, as condemned in al-Isra; they also claimed angels were God's daughters and likened human daughters to them.
rows.anchor: الخوف من لحوق العار بهم من أجلهم أو الخوف من الإملاق

rows.speaker: الفرزدق
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq boasts that his ancestor Sa'sa'a ibn Najiya prevented girls from being buried alive and saved the buried girls.
rows.anchor: وكان صعصعة بن ناجية ممن منع الوأد فافتخر الفرزدق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The victim is asked about her offense to shame her killer; Razi compares this to Jesus being asked whether he told people to worship him and his mother.
rows.anchor: سؤالها وجوابها تبكيب لقاتلها ، وهو كتبكيت النصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The active reading سألت can mean she argued for herself, asked God, or questioned her killer; قتلت is also read with a doubled consonant.
rows.anchor: قرئ سألت ، أي خاصمت عن نفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the famous reading is passive سئلت, its wording can imply that the killers are asked about her circumstances and what offense led to her death.
rows.anchor: تقدير الآية : وإذا الموءودة سئلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, a person may be asked about their own condition in the third person, as when Zayd is asked what he did.
rows.anchor: أن الإنسان قد يسأل عن حال نفسه عند المعاينة بلفظ المغايبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The records are read with a light or doubled consonant; they are deeds' scrolls, folded at a person's death and unfolded for accounting, or distributed among their owners.
rows.anchor: قرئ بالتخفيف والتشديد يريد صحف الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كشطت means uncovered and removed from what lies above it, Paradise and God's Throne, like stripping skin from a slaughtered animal or removing a cover.
rows.anchor: أي كشفت وأزيلت عما فوقها ، وهو الجنة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reads قشطت; al-Farra says it means stripped away and then folded, and the k/q alternation is common.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : قشطت ، واعتقاب القاف والكاف كثير ، يقال لبكت الثريد ولبقته ، والكافور والقافور ، قال الفراء : نزعت فطويت
